name: FLOWER BRAND · The Naira Reissue (पुनर्मुद्रण)
one_line: Twelve pieces of everyday Indian print a 35-to-54-year-old grew up inside, from the Doordarshan slate and the matchbox to the mithai lid and the wall calendar, reissued in Naira's own inks, where the jewellery is the only real, photographed thing on the page.
big_idea: Indian print was never meant to be precious: a matchbox label, a mithai-box lid, the Sivakasi cracker box, an inland letter, a notebook label, a wall calendar from the corner shop, the slate Doordarshan put up when the signal dropped. Everyone in Naira's audience grew up reading them. The Naira Reissue prints twelve of them again, faithfully in structure but only in Naira's inks (oxblood, aubergine, lilac, sage, blush, apricot, marigold, ivory), and in every frame the only full-colour, three-dimensional, photographed object is the piece. Flat ink, one real thing. The print format is the setup, the piece is the punchline, and one exact fact from the listing is the proof. Every Indian label carried a '___ Brand' trade mark (Ship Brand, Lion Brand); every reissue carries ours, FLOWER BRAND: the flower that stands as the I in NAIRA, set in a printer's oval. Three named series run through the grid like PTAT's MILNI: NAIRA TALKIES (screen and sound: the DD slate, the film poster, the cassette), DUKAAN (shop print: the earring card, the matchbox, the mithai lid, the cracker box) and KAAGAZ (household paper: the inland letter, the notebook label, the postage stamp, the wedding card, the wall calendar). It opens by owning the eleven-week silence with 'रुकावट के लिए खेद है', rides Karwa Chauth, Dhanteras, Diwali, Bhai Dooj and Children's Day, and closes on the wedding season with December's calendar page already full.
why_it_fits: BRAND: it turns Naira's existing assets up rather than borrowing PTAT's look. The flower mark becomes the recurring emblem; Velista caps plus a lowercase Cormorant turn stays the voice of every frame; the four camp palettes, the Red Room oxblood and the exhibition bottle green become the press inks; the bracketed [ piece · material · wink ] kicker closes every caption; numbered series (Nº 01–12) continue the house habit of N° capsules and Editions. It stays premium because the inks are limited, corners are sharp, the drawn print is crisp vector with only a whisper of grain and halftone, one idiom sits in each tile, and the only photographic thing is the product, true to the house constant that gold is the only saturated, dimensional element in frame. DATA: the account's best creative ever is a piece plus an everyday Indian object plus one witty Indian line plus one exact fact ('Anaar, pre-peeled.', Ruby Baguette Tennis Bracelet, ₹335 per purchase, ROAS 4.52); concept statics returned 1.44x against 0.57x for plain. Every reissue is that formula with a print object instead of a fruit. Women 35–54 placed 64% of purchases, and this is exactly the print they grew up with; Maharashtra is 46% of orders and Nashik 29 orders in 120 days, so the Marathi wall calendar, Devanagari numerals and Nashik Road's stamp press land at home. Feed and Stories stills earned 84% of purchases, so 8 of 12 posts are carousels or a single still and only 3 are reels (for reach on the relaunch, the box and the two-metal bangle). Every hero is in deep stock (19 to 79 units), led by the five pieces that sell in both ads and Shopify: Woven Gold Hoops (20 units, #1), Prism Rivière (#1 revenue), Baguette Tennis Bracelet (13 since 16 Oct, Ruby 8), Heartbead (11) and Brushed Gold Huggies (8), plus Edition Two pieces with stock but no sales yet (Baguette Tennis Necklace 70 in stock and 0 sold, Kiss Knot 40/0, Silk Mesh 40/0). Posting slots follow Shopify: Sunday is 27% of orders, peaks at 12:00, 18:00 and 21:00 IST. Offers live only in captions, as the exact BUY2/BUY3 line, never on Diwali day. OWNER TASTE: Indian everyday-object wit with restraint (the 12-tile caption system: one deadpan joke, the tile is the setup, the caption the second beat); nostalgia that loves aunties and mothers rather than mocking them; lilac (P3, P8 and P10's envelope), moody night grounds (oxblood, aubergine, bottle green), chic one-object compositions, exact facts and accuracy; no black, no beige, no clutter, no stickers, no soan papdi, no lyrics, no full faces. REFERENCE: it is PTAT's system translated: a recurring lockup on every cover (their MILNI hand-and-marigold, our FLOWER BRAND seal and slug), named series in waves (their event block, our festive wave through rows 4 to 2 and the wedding wave in row 1), Indian vernacular graphics used as quotation, one idiom per tile (their truck-art, block print, Rekha poster and steel thali; our DD slate, film poster, matchbox, mithai lid, Sivakasi label, inland letter, stamp, wedding card, calendar), multi-script type (Devanagari in every frame), real product dropped into a drawn world (their wardrobe and steel tray, our earring card and matchbox drawer), and grounds big enough that the grid reads as a colour rhythm. PTAT's Rekha F.O.M.O tile is answered directly by P2's painted film poster, with the piece as the star instead of an actress. Self-score on the igfinder grid rubric: cohesion 3, production 3 if built to spec, niche fit 3 (jewellery is the hero of every tile), proof 1 (packaging reel, worn slides, exact facts) = 10/10.

Cover headline meant to be read in the grid: 84 to 230 px (reads at 30 to 83 px in the 36% tile); inner-slide titles 64 to 120 px; tracking 0 to 0.06em; balanced, max two lines. CORMORANT GARAMOND ITALIC 400 (FEED/kit/fonts/CormorantGaramond-VF-italic-latin.woff2): the lowercase aside, 30 to 52 px, a complete sentence ending in a full stop. JOST 400/500 (FEED/kit/fonts/Jost-VF-latin.woff2): eyebrows, credits, fact lines and the slug; caps tracked 0.18 to 0.42em at 16 to 34 px; sentence-case facts 22 to 34 px, line height 1.4. POPPINS 500: the ₹ glyph only, via the tokens.css stack (prices are Jost 500 with Poppins fallback). TIRO DEVANAGARI MARATHI 400: exactly one Devanagari line per frame plus पुनर्मुद्रण in the slug, 16 to 96 px. KALAM 400 (not a brand face, owner sign-off needed, see risks): handwriting only, always in DEEP LILAC #4E3C66 as ballpoint ink, 18 to 52 px, each line rotated between −4° and +3°. Not used anywhere: Rozha One, Yatra One, Playfair Display, DM Serif Display, Gotu. Hierarchy on every cover: one Velista headline, at most one Cormorant aside, at most two Jost support lines plus the slug, at most one Devanagari line. MISREGISTRATION (the two-pass print tell): only on four cover titles (P2 CHAND NIKLA., P3 DO CHOTI, P5 ASSORTED., P6 ANAR): the same text in a second ink placed behind, offset 4 to 6 px right and 4 to 5 px down, 100% opacity; never on body text, never on the slug.
grid_system.emblem_and_recurring_devices: 1. THE FLOWER BRAND SEAL (S-01), the series emblem, on every cover: an upright oval 110 x 136 px; outer stroke 3 px and inner stroke 1 px inset 7 px, both in the frame's ink; fill = the frame's paper colour; inside, FEED/kit/naira-flower.svg (currentColor = the ink) 88 px tall, centred; below it a flat ribbon 150 x 28 px with 10 px notched ends, overlapping the oval's foot by 12 px, filled with the ink, carrying 'FLOWER BRAND' in Jost 500 13 px, tracking 0.18em, paper colour. Where the print format itself has a trade mark (P4 matchbox, P5 mithai lid) the seal is drawn larger as that format's mark and the slug drops its own seal, so a frame never carries two flowers. The seal never shares a frame with the NAIRA wordmark. 2. FLAT INK, ONE REAL THING: everything drawn is flat vector in the press inks; the only photograph or cut-out in a frame is Naira jewellery or Naira's own packaging photography, always true to the listing (never AI-drawn, never recoloured, gold kept warm-neutral). Where the drawing exaggerates scale, a line says so ('SHOWN LARGER THAN IT IS', P2). 3. PRINT TEXTURE, KEPT QUIET: paper surfaces get AI-02 (ivory cotton-rag paper scan) on multiply at 20 to 40%; drawn colour fields may carry a halftone screen (radial dots, 5 px pitch, 3 to 8% of the ink); misregistration only on the four titles named in type_system. No glitter, no stickers, no tape, no postmark except P10's one first-day cancellation. 4. ONE DEVANAGARI LINE PER FRAME (multi-script nod to PTAT, kept to one line and verified by a native reader): रुकावट के लिए खेद है, चाँद निकला, अनार, अंतर्देशीय पत्र, डिसेंबर २०२६, मेरी मौसी की शादी में ज़रूर आना, and पुनर्मुद्रण on every slug. 5. HANDWRITING in DEEP LILAC ballpoint (Kalam) wherever the original format was filled in by hand: tape label, inland letter, notebook label, envelope address, calendar scribbles. 6. THE COLOPHON (archive card), the last slide of every carousel (template T-COL): ground IVORY #FBF3EC with AI-02 multiply 35%; wordmark FEED/kit/naira-wordmark-ink-blush.svg 380 px wide, centred, top at y 110; 'THE NAIRA REISSUE · Nº 07' Jost 500 22 px tracking 0.32em GOLD TEXT #80612A centred, baseline 260; hairline GOLD #C99A4C 1 px from x 140 to 940 at y 300; three entries left-aligned at x 140, max width 800: label (THE ORIGINAL / THE REISSUE / THE PIECE) Jost 500 20 px tracking 0.3em GOLD TEXT, body for ORIGINAL and REISSUE in Cormorant italic 40 px INK line height 50, body for THE PIECE in Jost 400 30 px INK line height 44 with the price in Jost 500; 44 px between entries; the bracket kicker in Cormorant italic 36 px OXBLOOD centred, baseline 1120; 'nairaflore.com · link in bio' Jost 400 24 px tracking 0.12em WARM GREY #6E6863 centred, baseline 1180; then the slug without a seal (rule unbroken from x 72 to 1008 at y 1262). 7. INNER-SLIDE SLUG: 1.5 px rule in the frame's ink from x 72 to 1008 at y 1262; left 'REISSUE Nº 07' Jost 500 22 px tracking 0.22em, baseline 1300; right the page count '2 / 3' Jost 500 22 px, right-aligned at x 1008; no seal. 8. THREE SERIES: NAIRA TALKIES (P1, P2, P8), DUKAAN (P3, P4, P5, P6), KAAGAZ (P7, P9, P10, P11, P12); the series name appears only in captions and colophons, the slug carries the format name. 9. grid_system.transition_to_existing_grid: The bottom row (P3, P2, P1 from left) lands directly on LAC / flower / BONE. It inverts the old row's values for a crisp seam: P3's light lilac card sits on LAC's oxblood, P2's dark aubergine poster sits on the bone flower tile, and P1's colour bars end in a full-width oxblood band (window y 940 to 1440) that runs straight into BONE's oxblood, so the old campaign reads as the programme that the Doordarshan slate interrupts, and the new grid begins exactly where the old one stopped. Type continues across the seam: LAC and BONE are cream high-contrast serif caps on oxblood, and the reissues set Velista caps in cream on the same oxblood. The top row (oxblood calendar, ivory card, bottle-green stamp) repeats the old row's dark-light-dark, so the twelve new tiles are framed between two D-L-D rows. During rollout three posts land each week, so the grid is perfectly aligned every Sunday night (after P3, P6, P9, P12); mid-week the newest row is one or two tiles short, which is unavoidable and harmless.
grid_system.pins: Zero pins for the whole rollout. Pinned posts sit ahead of the grid and would shift every planned row by one or two columns. If the owner later wants pins, pin a full row of three (the top row P12, P11, P10) or none.

posts.concept: After eleven weeks of silence, the grid comes back the way Doordarshan always did: the slate 'रुकावट के लिए खेद है', sorry for the interruption, over the test-card colour bars. The bars are reprinted in the four stone colours of the Baguette Huggies (ruby red, clear, emerald green, amethyst lilac) plus gold, sage and aubergine, so the test signal is Edition Two's colour range. The joke: normal programming resumes, in four colours. In the grid it sits directly above the old BONE tile, the hinge between the old broadcast and the new.

posts.caption:
Rukavat ke liye khed hai. We were away for eleven weeks, and Doordarshan taught us how to come back.

The test card, reprinted in the four colours of the Baguette Huggies: ruby red, clear, emerald green and amethyst lilac. Small gold-tone hoops, about 18 mm across, with one row of baguette cubic zirconia along the front. ₹1,199 a pair.

Can't pick a channel? Take two pairs and wear one of each. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off, with codes BUY2 and BUY3 at checkout.

posts.alt_text: A television test card reprinted in soft vertical bars of ivory, gold, sage, green, lilac, ruby red and plum. A cream slate in the middle reads, in Hindi and English, 'Sorry for the interruption. Normal programming resumes.' Below, on an oxblood band, four pairs of small gold huggie earrings set with a row of ruby-red, clear, green and lilac baguette stones.
posts.why: The account has been silent since 9 Aug while Meta spent about ₹2.07 lakh sending people to the profile; this relaunch post owns the gap with a joke the 35–54 buyer (64% of purchases) recognises instantly. It leads with Edition Two, the season's story: the week of 19–24 Oct was the account's best ever (34 purchases, ROAS 1.87, cost per purchase ₹854) and the Edition Two catalogue returned ROAS 3.07. Baguette Huggies are the entry point to the baguette family that sells (Baguette Tennis Bracelet 13 in 9 days, Ruby 8 of 13; Huggies Ruby 3 of 3 in orders), with deep stock (57) and four colours that make the test card literal; huggies over-index 1.6x among competitor bestsellers. The caption turns 'pick two colours' into a natural BUY2 basket (69% of orders are a single piece). Reel format for reach on the comeback; Tuesday 18:30 sits on the 18:00 order peak. Grid: above BONE, its oxblood foot continues the old row.

posts.why: Karwa Chauth is a husband-to-wife gifting moment that almost nobody in the category speaks to (1 of 24 competitors mentions it), and the paid campaign's Karwa Chauth frame uses a different piece and line (Halo Curve Ring, 'two stones that don't match'), so this does not duplicate it. Night grounds were 5 of the owner's 8 Phase 3 picks. It answers the reference's Rekha poster head-on, with the piece instead of a face. Posted Wednesday 18:00 so it lands before Thursday's moonrise without printing a contested date.

posts.caption:
In wedding season the wall calendar fills up before the month even starts. December, already written over.

Haldi, sangeet, reception: the Bold Nocturne trio, one piece for each. The chain, the bracelet and the drops share the same polished oval links, each with one link set in pavé.

Chain ₹1,799, bracelet ₹1,599, drops ₹1,299. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off, with codes BUY2 and BUY3 at checkout.

posts.alt_text: A wall calendar page hanging from a brass nail on an oxblood wall. At the top, a photograph of a bold gold-tone link chain with one sparkling pavé link worn at an open shirt collar; below, DECEMBER in English and Marathi and a date grid scribbled over in violet ballpoint: haldi, mehendi, shaadi underlined twice, reception, sangeet in Pune, cocktail, gas booked. The footer reads 'With best compliments from Naira Petite.'
posts.why: The top-left tile is the first thing a visitor from a late-November ad sees, so it carries the season they are shopping for. The Bold Nocturne trio is deep stock (53, 49, 19) with few sales, and it has already been bought as a full BUY3 set (#1134); one piece per function makes a 3-piece basket feel natural, which matters because single-item baskets do not pay back (break-even ROAS 1.95). The Marathi calendar speaks to the 46% of buyers in Maharashtra. Sunday noon is the strongest order slot (27% of orders on Sundays). As the loud corner tile it echoes LAC's oxblood at the opposite end of the grid.
posts.claims_check: Tags: chain and bracelet 18k Gold Tone Plated, Hypoallergenic, Tarnish Free, Waterproof; drops the same plus Edition Two. Claimed: chain with bold oval paperclip links, one link pavé-set with clear cubic zirconia (listing); drops a polished oval link on a post with a larger pavé link below, about 30 mm (listing); bracelet described only as 'bold gold-tone links, one set in pavé, with a lobster clasp' because its listing text ('thick flat curb link, 18 cm') conflicts with its photos and alt text (fix the listing); 18K gold tone plated, waterproof and tarnish free (tags). No muhurat or festival dates are claimed: the scribbles are a fictional household's plans, the only printed festival is Christmas (fixed). No calendar brand name (no Kalnirnay) is used. 'Pinky' is a generic nickname. Devanagari month and numerals need a native check.

risks: Devanagari lines (रुकावट के लिए खेद है, चाँद निकला, अनार, अंतर्देशीय पत्र, डिसेंबर २०२६, मेरी मौसी की शादी में ज़रूर आना, पुनर्मुद्रण) must be checked glyph by glyph by a native Hindi and Marathi reader in the final renders; a broken conjunct in Tiro would undo the premium read.
Kalam is not a brand face. It is used only for handwriting (five posts) and always in deep lilac; it needs the owner's sign-off, or a real handwriting scan from someone at the studio can replace it.

The flower is promoted from a 6–15% ghost to a solid emblem (the FLOWER BRAND seal). The brand bible leaves this to the owner for the feed; the rule here is that the seal never shares a frame with the wordmark. If the owner says no, the seal becomes an oval with the word FLOWER BRAND only.

Ruby stock is thin: the Baguette Tennis Bracelet in Ruby had 12 on 25 Oct and sells about one a day. P6 (8 Nov) has a stock guard (under 6 means swap to the Ruby necklace, 20 in stock). P1 mentions Ruby huggies (12).
Prices drifted three times in October. Prices appear only on colophon, end-card and price-card slides and in captions; re-read Shopify on each posting day and re-render those slides only.

Nostalgia formats borrow public idioms, not property: no Doordarshan or India Post logos, no State Emblem, no real film title or actor likeness, no Kalnirnay or cassette or firecracker brand names, the stamp says NASHIK and has no rupee value. Still, have someone read every frame for anything that could look like an official document.

Kitsch risk: the angle is maximal in idea. Hold the line in execution: only the listed inks, misregistration on four titles only, grain at 20–40%, no glitter, stickers or extra stamps, one idiom per tile. If a render looks like a costume, cut ornament before adding anything.

'Sorry for the interruption' openly acknowledges the eleven-week silence. Most will read it as charm; if the owner prefers not to mention the gap, the slate keeps the Devanagari line and the English becomes 'NORMAL PROGRAMMING RESUMES.'
A firecracker reference on Diwali day in a pollution-ban year: the copy deliberately says 'no smoke, no noise' and nothing is lit on screen, but it is still a sensitivity worth a second look.

Facts to confirm before posting: one box per piece ('exact contents: 1', P4); India Security Press, Nashik Road prints postage stamps (P10 wording); 'most-ordered' claims (Woven Gold Hoops overall, Ruby among the bracelet's colours) on posting day; the Bold Nocturne Bracelet's listing text (curb link, 18 cm) disagrees with its photos, so the copy avoids link type and length and the listing should be fixed.

Three reels (P1, P4, P8): ad data says reels sold reach, not baskets (10% of purchases from 72% of impressions). They are here for reach and motion with a purpose; the selling is done by the carousels.
Mid-week the grid is one or two tiles out of alignment; it is perfect every Sunday night. No pins.

Scale: P1's video frames, P2's poster and P8's cassette show pieces larger than life. P1 and P2 say so on screen; the cassette's oversized bangles are an obvious graphic device, but if the owner wants it, add 'SHOWN LARGER' to its credits too.
